title: Special Topics in Film Production: Glitch Art
description: Students learn critical methods and techniques of digital media production through the lens of the glitch. The class structure consists of design, lectures, and design critiques where students produce glitched images, soundscapes, 3D objects, videos, and collaborative projects. The concept and creation of the glitch continue to engage artists and theorists working across different arts disciplines, and in particular visual arts, digital art, music, and sonic art. Celebrated as a productive, generative figure within art practice, and also as a disruptive, destabilizing form with radical potential, the glitch celebrates faults, failures, malfunctions, disturbances, anomalies, bugs, errors, and noise.
prerequisites_raw: Film Studies 46; and, consent of instructor.

title: Motion Graphics
description: This studio course focuses on motion graphics and aesthetic interdisciplinary animation using graphics, typography, computer/video visual imaging and sound synthesis. Projects will cover basic motion graphics principles, design and composition, timing and drama, storyboarding and planning, sound and music development and synchronization.
prerequisites_raw: Film Studies 46; and, consent of instructor.

title: Media 4 Nonprofits
description: This course equips students with a mixture of production skills in 3D modeling, data visualization, gaming, mixed realities, and digital video, tailored to create compelling content for local nonprofit organizations. The curriculum integrates context with content creation, storytelling, media activism, AI applications, and ethical collaboration, preparing students for impactful careers in the nonprofit sector and beyond. This class bridges academic learning with real-world application, empowering students to build critical portfolios and professional networks.
prerequisites_raw: Film Studies 46; and, consent of instructor.
